- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overcorrects downward — reduce forecast slope to avoid overshoot.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from peak), model overestimates continuation — adjust downward with steeper decay.  
- In low-sentiment periods (sentiment ≤0.1), model often underestimates volatility — add 2–5% buffer to forecast to account for hidden risk.  
- Model consistently underpredicts true price peaks in 30-day horizon — apply upward bias of 3–8% for high-sentiment or post-spike periods.  
- If sentiment history shows rising optimism (e.g., 0.2→0.5→0.8), model lags in adjusting — delay forecast rise by 1–2 days or add early momentum buffer.
